text:
Maria: Quick helm question — our chart uses an emptyMap for env and when I --set to add a single env var it seems to replace the whole block and remove envFrom.secretRef. Is that expected?

Example values.yaml:
```yaml
container:
  env: {}
  envFrom:
    - secretRef:
        name: svc-credentials
```

Command I run: `helm upgrade --install svc ./chart --set container.env[0].name=FEATURE_FLAG --set container.env[0].value=true`

Result: rendered pod no longer has envFrom.

Sandeep: Yeah, this is Helm/Go template merge semantics — when you set a value for `container.env` (an array/map) via `--set`, Helm treats that as replacing the entire key. Empty map vs null sometimes changes whether templates consider the key present. Short answer: explicit --set replaces.

Oliver: To add: you can handle this in the template rather than relying on caller behavior. We solved it by adding a small merge helper in _helpers.tpl and guarding envFrom. Example snippet I used: 
```gotpl
{{- $base := default (dict) .Values.container.env -}}
{{- $extras := .Values.container.extraEnv | default (dict) -}}
{{- $merged := merge $base $extras -}}
env: {{ toYaml $merged | nindent 8 }}
```
For arrays you'll need append/concat logic instead of merge. Also `env: null` in values.yaml will make the template treat it as absent and avoid accidental replacement.

Tyler: Another pattern: expose `extraEnv` or `userEnv` explicitly so callers do `--set container.extraEnv[0].name=FOO` and template composes them. Keeps overrides explicit and avoids surprising wipes.

Maria: Good tips. If I add `extraEnv` and use merge in the template, do we still need to change callers? I want existing CI deploy script to be able to `--set container.env[...]` for quick debug without breaking secret refs.

Sandeep: If you want backward compat then in template do: `{{- $env := merge (default (dict) .Values.container.env) (default (dict) .Values.container.extraEnv) }}` and document that `--set container.env` will replace only user-visible keys if they exist, but `extraEnv` is preferred for layering. Might be easier to treat `env` as primary and only append secret-backed envFrom in template (i.e., render envFrom unconditionally unless values explicitly disable it).

infra-bot: FYI I'll be changing the deploy script in staging later today to add a safeguard flag that uses `--set` for `container.extraEnv` instead of `container.env` so we don't wipe secret refs during on-call debug. Scheduled at 20:00 UTC.

Maria: OK I'll try the merge helper + extraEnv and open a tiny PR to chart to add the helper and update docs. Thanks!

deploy-bot: CI will run on the PR; once green we can test on staging. :white_check_mark:
